question.problem:
Let $D$ be the finite region bounded by the curve 
$({x}^{3}-y)^{4}-y=1$ and the line $y=2.$ Consider the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where $u={x}^{3}-y$ and $v=y.$ Find the representation of ${T}^{-1}(D)$ in the $uv$-plane.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that we are given that 

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}-y \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

Substituting ${x}^{3}-y=u$ and $y=v$ into the equation of the first curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}^{3}-y)^{4}-y=1\,⟹\,{u}^{4}-v=1\,⟹\,v={u}^{4}-1,\end{aligned}
$$

while substituting $y=v$ into the equation of the second curve, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y=2\,⟹\,v=2.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the intersections of the curves in the $uv$-plane, we solve the following system:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}v={u}^{4}-1 \\ v=2\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}u=\pm \sqrt[4]{3} \\ v=2.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection points are $(\pm \sqrt[4]{3},2).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14166956/assets/5a2e3fd6f3669f38834359f69e68b01a1e0d1438023418c5234d4071182f4808.png)

As a result, our domain in the $uv$-plane has the type I representation 

$$
{T}^{-1}(D)=\{(u,v)\,:\,-\sqrt[4]{3}\le u\le \sqrt[4]{3},\,{u}^{4}-1\le v\le 2\}.
$$
